title: Contributions of individual muscles to the submental surface electromyogram during swallowing
what_they_did: Recorded submental surface EMG simultaneously with intramuscular EMG from mylohyoid, anterior digastric, geniohyoid, genioglossus and platysma during swallowing and modelled each muscle's contribution.
useful_for_us: Establishes what a hidden submental electrode actually sees: mylohyoid, anterior belly of digastric and geniohyoid dominate, while genioglossus and platysma contribute minimally.

title: Neck and face surface electromyography for prosthetic voice control after total laryngectomy
what_they_did: Compared neck and face sEMG recording locations for controlling an electrolarynx in eight laryngectomy speakers producing serial and running speech.
useful_for_us: Names the best control locations as the superior ventral neck or submental surface, direct support that concealed under-jaw and neck sites carry usable volitional speech-muscle signals.

title: Development of a speech-discriminating electromyogram system for routine ambulatory recordings for the low-level masseter muscle activity
what_they_did: Built an ambulatory masseter EMG system with a voice sensor to separate speech from low-level clenching and validated it in 16 subjects.
useful_for_us: Shows speech and low-level masseter activity can be discriminated (R-squared 0.9935 for speech duration), a needed guard for a jaw-channel system that must not mistake everyday talking artefacts for commands.

title: An Optimal Set of Flesh Points on Tongue and Lips for Speech-Movement Classification
what_they_did: Used two electromagnetic articulographs to record tongue and lip movements from 13 talkers and compared sensor-subset classification accuracies.
useful_for_us: The four flesh points T1, T4, upper lip and lower lip matched the full six-sensor set at 91-95%, the clearest articulography precedent for finding a minimal sensor subset.

title: Temporary-tattoo for long-term high fidelity biopotential recordings
what_they_did: Screen-printed carbon temporary-tattoo electrodes with plasma-polymerised PEDOT and measured impedance and EMG on the hand and face.
useful_for_us: Reports a 10-fold impedance reduction on skin and a 100-fold capacitance increase, the quantitative basis for expecting tattoo electrodes to work on facial skin.

title: Silent Speech Recognition as an Alternative Communication Device for Persons with Laryngectomy
what_they_did: Recorded 8 sEMG sensors (4 face, 4 neck) from 8 laryngectomy speakers reading phrases from a 2,500-word vocabulary and trained phoneme-based recognisers.
useful_for_us: Gives the classic subset cost: 10.3% WER with all 8 sensors versus 13.6% reduced to 4 per speaker, so halving the montage costs about 3 WER points.

title: Ultraconformable Temporary Tattoo Electrodes for Electrophysiology
what_they_did: Inkjet-printed conducting-polymer temporary-tattoo electrodes under 1 micrometre thick and characterised skin-contact impedance over 1 hour and 48 hours, validating facial sEMG and ECG.
useful_for_us: 48-hour impedance and facial sEMG validation make the tattoo route credible for multi-day hidden under-jaw recording.

title: Speaker-Independent Silent Speech Recognition from Flesh-Point Articulatory Movements Using an LSTM Neural Network
what_they_did: Collected tongue and lip flesh-point data with an electromagnetic articulograph from twelve healthy and two laryngectomy speakers and tested speaker-independent silent speech recognition with articulatory normalisation.
useful_for_us: Documents the normalisation pipeline that makes articulatory data transfer across speakers and confirms laryngectomy speakers can be decoded from the same flesh points.

title: Neuromechanical Modelling of Articulatory Movements from Surface Electromyography and Speech Formants
what_they_did: Recorded masseter surface EMG and acoustic formants during speech and correlated dynamic muscle behaviour with jaw and tongue kinematic variables.
useful_for_us: Quantifies that a single masseter channel tracks first-formant jaw kinematics, supporting the jaw line as a hidden site that carries articulation information.

title: Validation of Polymer-Based Screen-Printed Textile Electrodes for Surface EMG Detection
what_they_did: Screen-printed PEDOT:PSS textile electrodes on cotton and compared noise, impedance and sEMG waveform shape with gelled electrodes across dry, hydrogel and saline conditions and two sizes.
useful_for_us: Textile electrodes matched gel electrodes with hydrogel or saline (waveform correlation above 97%) and worked for 35 minutes while walking, giving realistic dry-versus-gel expectations.

title: Highly Porous Platinum Electrodes for Dry Ear-EEG Measurements
what_they_did: Laser-patterned personalised porous platinum electrodes for dry in-ear EEG, increasing effective surface area 40-fold, and measured the Berger effect from one ear.
useful_for_us: Dry ear electrodes with surface-area engineering matched gel Ag/AgCl signal-to-noise ratio, the materials precedent for a gel-free ear pod.

title: Silent Speech Decoding Using Spectrogram Features Based on Neuromuscular Activities
what_they_did: Converted mouthed-speech sEMG into spectrograms and compared MLP, CNN and bidirectional LSTM decoders for word recognition.
useful_for_us: Confirms mouthed (silently articulated) sEMG carries decodable word information, with BiLSTM at 90%, and shows spectrogram features are a simple baseline for our own channel-subset comparisons.

title: Towards optimizing electrode configurations for silent speech recognition based on high-density surface electromyography
what_they_did: Placed 120 closely spaced high-density sEMG electrodes on the face and neck and used sequential forward selection to find optimal electrode subsets for classifying ten silently spoken digits in English and Chinese.
useful_for_us: Directly quantifies the hidden-site payoff: 10 optimised electrodes matched 40 non-optimised ones (86% English, 94% Chinese), and the selected sites fell mostly on the neck rather than the face.

title: Intrinsic Laryngeal Muscle Activity During Subvocalization
what_they_did: Used fine-wire EMG to measure intrinsic laryngeal muscle activity during silent reading tasks in 45 women, with submental surface EMG in two of the experiments.
useful_for_us: A caution for subvocal-only decoding: intrinsic laryngeal responses to subvocalisation were small and idiosyncratic (only right cricothyroid significant), so thinking the words may not drive hidden larynx channels.

title: Speech-imagery-based brain-computer interface system using ear-EEG
what_they_did: Compared a wearable ear-EEG system with a 32-channel scalp EEG setup on a four-class speech-imagery task in ten subjects across six sessions.
useful_for_us: Ear-EEG averaged 38.2% versus 43.1% for scalp EEG and seven of ten subjects showed no significant difference, a realistic ceiling for imagining speech with a concealed ear device.

title: Surface Electromyography-Based Recognition, Synthesis, and Perception of Prosodic Subvocal Speech
what_they_did: Recorded face and neck sEMG from 4 laryngectomy and 4 control speakers subvocally reciting 750 phrases, synthesised personalised voices and ran listener tests.
useful_for_us: A rare measurement of both lexical and prosodic decoding from the same face and neck sEMG (96.3% lexical, 91.2% stress) plus how naive listeners rate the synthesised output.

title: Design and Characterization of a Textile Electrode System for the Detection of High-Density sEMG
what_they_did: Designed and characterised a 32-electrode, 15 mm-spacing textile HD-sEMG grid and tested it in static and dynamic contractions.
useful_for_us: Demonstrates a large-format textile HD array with a stable electrode-skin interface during movement, the kind of matrix needed to map hidden neck sites.

title: An epidermal sEMG tattoo-like patch as a new human-machine interface for patients with loss of voice
what_they_did: Made a below-10-micrometre epidermal sEMG tattoo-like patch that records from three jaw and face muscle channels and classified silent action and emotion instructions.
useful_for_us: One of the few silent-speech demonstrations with an epidermal patch: 89.04% action and 92.33% emotion accuracy, including a channel under the jaw.

title: Parallel-Inception CNN Approach for Facial sEMG based Silent Speech Recognition
what_they_did: Designed a 100-class daily-demand data set from facial sEMG and a Parallel-Inception CNN using log Mel-frequency spectral coefficients.
useful_for_us: 88.44% on a 100-word facial sEMG set gives the upper bound for a face-only (partly visible) montage, the number a hidden subset must be compared against.

title: Pterygoid muscle activity in speech: A preliminary investigation
what_they_did: Made intramuscular EMG recordings from the medial and lateral pterygoid muscles in five speakers producing 40 nonsense words and timed their activation to consonants and vowels.
useful_for_us: Shows the deep jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles have distinct, speech-locked activity patterns, useful anatomy for deciding which surface sites can proxy them.

title: Ultrathin crystalline-silicon-based strain gauges with deep learning algorithms for silent speech interfaces
what_they_did: Fabricated ultrathin crystalline-silicon strain gauges under 0.1 mm-squared and attached four near the mouth to classify 100 silently spoken words with a 3D convolutional network.
useful_for_us: 87.53% on 100 words versus 42.60% for a same-size sEMG electrode shows that non-EMG mechanical sensing can beat surface EMG on a visible lip montage.

title: Electromyogram-Based Lip-Reading via Unobtrusive Dry Electrodes and Machine Learning Methods
what_they_did: Developed self-adhesive, skin-conformable, semi-transparent dry electrodes and decoded lip-movement sEMG for viseme recognition in noisy and dark conditions.
useful_for_us: Shows an unobtrusive skin-like electrode can capture speech-relevant EMG around the lips and stay robust to environment, though the lip montage is not concealable.

title: A Novel Screen-Printed Textile Interface for High-Density Electromyography Recording
what_they_did: Screen-printed a dry high-density EMG electrode matrix on textile with a soft polymer coating and benchmarked it against PET/hydrogel electrodes on hand gestures.
useful_for_us: Textile and hydrogel HD-EMG gave similar spectra, magnitude, spatial distribution and signal-to-noise ratio and similar gesture performance, supporting textile electrodes in a washable face or neck garment.

title: Decoding Silent Speech Based on High-Density Surface Electromyogram Using Spatiotemporal Neural Network
what_they_did: Used four 64-channel HD-sEMG arrays over facial and laryngeal muscles in fifteen subjects subvocalising 33 Chinese phrases (82 syllables) and decoded with a spatio-temporal end-to-end network.
useful_for_us: Strongest syllable-level silent result found (97.17% phrase accuracy, 3.11% character error) and it again places large arrays partly on the larynx/neck, supporting hidden neck coverage.

title: MagTrack: A Wearable Tongue Motion Tracking System for Silent Speech Interfaces
what_they_did: Validated MagTrack, a wearable electromagnetic articulograph, for vowel classification and continuous silent speech recognition against a commercial articulograph.
useful_for_us: 89.74% vowel classification with a wearable tracker and comparable phoneme error rates to the commercial system, evidence that wearable articulography as well as EMG can decode silent articulation.

title: Bio-potential noise of dry printed electrodes: physiology versus the skin-electrode impedance
what_they_did: Measured the noise of dry printed electrodes on the arm and face and related it to skin-electrode impedance and physiological state.
useful_for_us: Facial dry-electrode noise exceeded the Nyquist prediction from impedance, so facial dry arrays need empirical noise characterisation rather than impedance alone.

title: Decoding silent speech commands from articulatory movements through soft magnetic skin and machine learning
what_they_did: Placed a single soft magnetic skin behind the ear to track temporomandibular joint motion and decoded silent speech commands with machine learning.
useful_for_us: A single hidden behind-the-ear sensor reached 93.2% on phonemes and 87.3% on words, the strongest existence proof that a concealed non-EMG sensor behind the ear can carry word-level silent speech.

title: A simplified adversarial architecture for cross-subject silent speech recognition using electromyography
what_they_did: Proposed a discrepancy-based adversarial network for cross-subject EMG silent-speech recognition, evaluated on 100 Chinese sentences with 60 training and 40 new subjects.
useful_for_us: Quantifies cross-subject generalisation (89.46% on unseen subjects) and the feature-alignment tricks that let calibration transfer, which matters for a one-person system built from borrowed recordings.

title: Speech synthesis from three-axis accelerometer signals using conformer-based deep neural network
what_they_did: Attached four optimised plus one additional three-axis accelerometer to the face and chin and synthesised Korean speech from 270 sentences with a Conformer model.
useful_for_us: The extra accelerometer under the chin significantly improved spectral quality (mel cepstral distortion 5.03 to 4.86), direct evidence that a hidden under-chin motion sensor adds information.

title: Prosodic Preferences of Surface Electromyography-based Subvocal Speech for People With Laryngectomy
what_they_did: Surveyed 15 laryngectomy patients and 5 communication partners on synthesised prosody and ranked the features of a silent-speech aid.
useful_for_us: User ranking puts sound quality, intelligibility and pitch first and wearability, training, cost and visibility last, so concealment matters less than intelligibility to the intended user group.

title: Electrode Setup for Electromyography-Based Silent Speech Interfaces: A Pilot Study
what_they_did: Ran multiple pilot recording sessions with paired and concentric electrodes at different face and neck muscles and scored frame-level phone classification to fix the electrode setup for a laryngectomy EMG-audio database.
useful_for_us: Gives an explicit eight-channel set (digastric, depressor anguli oris, risorius, levator labii superioris, masseter, zygomaticus major, depressor labii superioris, stylohyoid); four of the eight sit below the jaw line and are concealable.

title: In-Ear System for Monitoring Lower Jaw Motion: A Novel Approach to Speech Intention Detection in Laryngectomy Patients
what_they_did: Built a 3D-printed in-ear device with four infrared proximity sensors to measure outer-ear-canal deformation from jaw motion and validated onset and offset against sEMG and audio.
useful_for_us: Establishes the ear canal as a discreet, reproducible sensor site for jaw movement and speech intention, with no skin electrodes on the face.

title: emg2vec: Self-supervised Pretraining in Electromyography-based Silent Speech Interfaces
what_they_did: Pretrained a self-supervised emg2vec encoder for EMG-to-text and EMG-to-speech and compared it against training from scratch.
useful_for_us: Reports a 7.32% relative WER improvement from self-supervised pretraining on the full labelled set and 5.18% on 20% of labels, a cheap way to exploit unlabelled recording time.

title: A Wearable Silent Text Input System Using EMG and Piezoelectric Sensors
what_they_did: Combined an EMG sensor and a PZT piezoelectric sensor in a chin-mounted unit and classified the eight most frequent English letters over 100 trials each.
useful_for_us: 95.63% from a single chin-worn module mixing muscle and mechanical signals is a concrete hidden-site design point for a first prototype.

title: Geometry of orofacial neuromuscular signals: speech articulation decoding using surface electromyography
what_they_did: Collected surface EMG from face, jaw and neck during speech and showed that the symmetric positive-definite matrix manifold is a natural embedding space, analysing cross-individual distribution shift.
useful_for_us: Provides a principled cross-subject alignment method for the face/jaw/neck montage we intend to record and confirms jaw and neck channels are part of a working decoding set.

title: Exploring Muscle Synergy Consistency and Physiological Interpretability in Speech Evaluation Using High-Density sEMG
what_they_did: Recorded high-density sEMG with five electrode arrays over face, jaw and neck from ten participants performing 14 vowel and 15 consonant tasks in phonated and silent modes, then extracted muscle synergies.
useful_for_us: Three synergies reconstructed activation with over 95% variance and synergy features pushed classification to 94.72%, evidence that a few spatial components rather than dozens of electrodes carry the speech information.

title: The speech reception threshold can be estimated using EEG electrodes in and around the ear
what_they_did: Estimated the speech reception threshold from 66 scalp and 12 ear EEG electrodes in 20 normal-hearing participants using envelope reconstruction.
useful_for_us: In-ear electrodes alone estimated the threshold within 3 dB for only 30% of participants, but combining in-ear and around-ear reached 95%, so ear decoding should use both regions.

title: Sentence-Level Silent Speech Recognition Using a Wearable EMG/EEG Sensor System with AI-Driven Sensor Fusion and Language Model
what_they_did: Built a wearable system with one EMG and one EEG channel and a Siamese few-shot moving-window model plus a statistical language model, tested on four command sentences of ten words.
useful_for_us: Demonstrates that a single hidden EMG channel plus a single EEG channel reaches 95.25% sentence accuracy with language-model rescoring, the low-channel-count end of the design space.

title: A Dual-Modal Silent Speech Interface via Surface Electromyography (sEMG) and Vibration Sensing
what_they_did: Built a dual-modal throat interface pairing PVA/PAA hydrogel sEMG electrodes (270 ohm at 1 kHz) with a 28 micrometre PVDF vibration sensor and fused them in a dual-branch network.
useful_for_us: Shows a hydrogel electrode on the throat can record silent-speech EMG at low impedance and that adding a vibration channel improves recognition, a route to keeping every sensor under the collar.

title: Aesthetic Experience in the Acceptance of Wearable Technology for People With Dementia: Critical Interpretive Synthesis
what_they_did: Critical interpretive synthesis of 63 studies on how the aesthetic design of wearables relates to acceptance in dementia care.
useful_for_us: Evidence that aesthetically considered, comfortable and personally meaningful wearables are accepted more readily, a counterweight to purely technical concealment arguments.

title: A direct comparison of simultaneously recorded scalp, around-ear and in-ear EEG for neural selective auditory attention decoding to speech
what_they_did: Recorded scalp, around-ear and in-ear EEG simultaneously during selective auditory attention to speech and compared decoding accuracies.
useful_for_us: Gives the ear-site ordering for the same task: scalp 83.4%, around-ear 67.2%, in-ear 61.1%, and shows adding a few scalp or external-reference electrodes buys over 10 points.

title: Large-scale training data enhances silent speech decoding with around-ear EEG
what_they_did: Collected 72 hours of around-ear EEG from 24 healthy participants and one locked-in participant during silent, vocalised and attempted speech and pooled them with prior EMG and high-density EEG data.
useful_for_us: Around-ear EEG alone reached 56.6% (healthy) and 47.3% (locked-in) on 64 words and fine-tuning added 22 points, defining what ear-only decoding currently delivers.

title: Turning glasses into sensors: capacitive facial expression recognition under frame geometry constraints
what_they_did: Integrated eight capacitive sensing channels into ordinary eyeglass frames (FERGlasses) and validated facial action-unit monitoring against optical and computer-vision baselines, with channel ablation.
useful_for_us: Demonstrates a genuinely inconspicuous glasses form factor and quantifies which frame electrode groups drive upper-face and cheek signals; lower-face and chin signals attenuate (cosine 0.33).

title: Electrospun Surface-Modified Epidermal Strain Sensors Enable Silent Speech and Hand Gesture Recognition for Virtual Reality Interaction
what_they_did: Fabricated electrospun surface-modified epidermal strain sensors (gauge factor up to 243) in a seven-channel array and decoded silent speech and hand gestures with a CNN-Transformer network.
useful_for_us: Over 98% silent-speech accuracy from a seven-channel epidermal strain array, another skin-like mechanical route with the array placed on the face.

title: Ultrathin Temporary Tattoo Electrodes Enable Prolonged Skin-Conformable EMG Sensing for Hip Exoskeleton Control
what_they_did: Compared ultrathin temporary-tattoo EMG electrodes with gel electrodes on four leg muscles during treadmill walking and re-tested after eight hours of wear.
useful_for_us: No significant signal-quality difference from gel (RMSE 0.069, correlation 0.844) and no degradation after 8 hours, the strongest duration evidence for tattoo EMG, though measured on the leg rather than the face.

title: A Wearable Earplug-Shaped Piezoresistive Sensor Based on Ear Canal Deformation for the Screening of Temporomandibular Joint Motion Abnormalities
what_they_did: Made an rGO composite aerogel piezoresistive earbud that senses anterior ear-canal deformation, characterised it (14.5 Pa threshold, 64 ms response) and classified jaw-motion patterns with an SVM.
useful_for_us: 91.7% classification of temporomandibular joint motion patterns from a single in-ear sensor, another hidden ear-canal signal for jaw-related decoding.

title: Reduction of appearance artifacts in wearable on-skin electronics
what_they_did: Developed fully invisible and unperceivable on-skin electrodes, confirmed with sensory experiments and physical characterisation, and recorded facial EOG, EMG and EEG.
useful_for_us: Directly addresses the concealment requirement: neither wearer nor observers could detect the electrodes visually or by touch, and wearers' psychological measures were unaffected.

title: Noninvasive Speech Restoration After Total Laryngectomy Using Surface Electromyography: Pilot Study
what_they_did: Recorded sEMG from a 20-electrode face, jaw and neck montage in one laryngectomy patient and one healthy speaker silently articulating 499 dates and times, then selected a reduced electrode subset and measured human-listener WER.
useful_for_us: Explicit subset result: 9 of 20 electrodes (11 of 18 for the reference speaker) captured 95% of the multi-channel signal, with WER 20.2% for the patient and 14.9% for the reference.

title: Skin-Conformal Inertial Sensing Interface for Continuous Silent Speech Recognition
what_they_did: Integrated commercial inertial measurement units on a skin-conformal substrate for lip articulation and used sliding-window decoding for continuous silent speech.
useful_for_us: 99.6% on a 25-word discrete vocabulary and 92.5% on untrained sequences show a thin conformal inertial interface can do continuous decoding, but the lip-mounted form factor is visible.

title: Procedures for verification of electrode placement in EMG studies of orofacial and mandibular muscles
what_they_did: Recorded EMG from 18 orofacial and mandibular muscles during muscle-specific gestures and documented anatomical criteria for verifying electrode placement and signal differentiation.
useful_for_us: A practical placement and verification checklist for the small, closely packed jaw muscles whose signals must be separated when choosing among hidden chin sites.
